title: Per-model request-quality declaration and Bayesian error-escrow playbook
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Purpose: Define a per-model and per-endpoint request-quality SLI signature and an associated Bayesian error-escrow mechanism to power automated circuit calibration, multi-region shedding decisions, and tenant-aware graceful degradation.

Background: Current SLI work at Redwood focuses on latency/availability percentiles and coarse quality labels. For models serving a mix of short and long requests, and for multi-tenant endpoints with heterogeneous value, we need a more expressive SLI that encodes request-level quality and a probabilistic error-budget forecast that supports soft-degradation decisions. This ticket collects requirements, a concrete SLI definition, burn-rate forecasting approach (Bayesian), and an operational playbook for automated shedding and circuit thresholds.

Proposal summary:
1) Request-Quality SLI: compute a single per-request score in [0,1] combining: prompt length and ratio to completion (length ratio), model-internal confidence proxy (e.g., token logprob delta or compressed-reconstruction perplexity), safety filter pass/fail penalty, and prompt-template match (for known golden flows). We normalize and weight components to produce a monotonic quality score. SLI for a route/model is the fraction of requests above a quality threshold (default 0.7) over a rolling window (e.g., 1h).

2) Bayesian Error-Escrow Ledger: model per-route error-budget as a probabilistic escrow rather than a fixed bucket. Maintain a prior on expected burn-rate per hour for each model-tenant pair (hierarchical model: global -> model -> tenant). Update posterior continuously with observed quality failures. Use posterior predictive to compute P(budget exhausted within N hours). The escrow can be fractional and supports temporary lending between low-risk tenants and higher-value tenants via explicit policies.

3) Automated circuit calibration: feed the Bayesian burn-rate signal into a Thompson-sampling-based controller that selects circuit thresholds (e.g., failover condition: P(budget_exhausted_in_2h) > 0.8) and shedding aggressiveness. The controller uses simulated trials on historical telemetry (offline replay) before applying changes.

4) Multi-region failover and shedding integration: When the posterior indicates regional resource stress, we evaluate cross-region redundancy: prefer routing to regions with higher remaining escrow. For pinned workloads the system attempts proportional shedding with tenant-weighted priorities.

Success criteria (high-level):
- Clear SLI definition implemented in telemetry pipeline and available in console for any route.
- Bayesian escrow computed per model, and burn-risk exposure visualized.
- Automatic circuit tuning enabled behind a feature flag for a small canary set of routes.
- No measurable increase in false-positive circuit trips during 72h canary (target <1%).

Deliverables:
- Canonical SLI spec document (this ticket) and a short Confluence page with examples.
- Telemetry implementation: SLI computation job + per-request quality tag in logs.
- Escrow service: lightweight posterior updater and API returning P(burn_in_N_hours).
- Controller: offline simulator + online actuator behind feature flag.
- Runbook: how to rollback and manual overrides.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Which confidence proxy to use across architectures (logprobs available for some models, not for others)? Fallback proposals: distillation-based reconstruction perplexity or ensemble agreement.
- How to weight tenant priority vs fairness? Initial policy: explicit tenant priority labels + capped borrowing.
- Window sizing: shorter windows react faster but increase variance. We'll expose window as a config per-route.

Monitoring and metrics to add:
- per-route: request_quality_distribution (histogram), quality_threshold_pass_rate (SLI), burn_rate_posterior_mean, burn_risk_p95, circuit_state_events, shed_percentage_by_tenant.
- Canary KPIs: circuit_trip_rate, false_positive_rate (customer-reported), customer_latencies and error rates pre/post-shedding.

Operational notes:
- Default thresholds conservative: feature-flagged auto-mode only for internal apps and select PLG routes for 2 weeks.
- All auto-actuation requires an audit log and operator email notification.

Implementation timeline (proposed):
- Week 1: finalize SLI formula and create confluence spec.
- Week 2: ingest per-request quality into telemetry pipeline (batch + streaming).
- Week 3: prototype Bayesian escrow updater and offline simulator.
- Week 4: run offline calibration and start closed-canary (read-only in dashboard).
- Week 5: enable feature-flagged actuation for internal routes, monitor 2 weeks, iterate.

Rollout gating criteria:
- Telemetry accuracy verified (synthetic prompts, golden flows).
- Posterior calibration checked: predicted burn frequency matches empirical within 10%.
- Stakeholder sign-off (SRE, Product, Security).
acceptance_criteria: SLI computed and visible in console for at least 3 representative routes (short-chat, long-generation, embedding) and matches offline computations
Bayesian escrow API returns posterior burn-risk metrics with <10% calibration error on historical fold
Offline simulator shows actuation reduces tail-unavailability during simulated overload without increasing overall error-rate for high-priority tenants
Audit logs record every auto-actuation and manual override; operator can rollback within 15 minutes
Canary run demonstrates false-positive circuit trips <1% over 72h
rollout_plan: 1) Create feature branch for telemetry and escrow service; 2) Deploy read-only escrow metrics to console behind feature flag; 3) Run offline simulator against last 90 days of telemetry; 4) Start internal canary (10 internal routes) with auto-actuation disabled; 5) Enable auto-actuation for internal canary with strict thresholds and alerting; 6) Expand to PLG routes and schedule 2-week observation before enabling for customer-facing highest-priority tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for SLI scoring components; integration tests that inject synthetic requests covering boundary conditions; posterior calibration tests using k-fold backtests; end-to-end canary tests that validate circuit decisions against known stress traces. Include chaos test that simulates regional outage and verifies proportional shedding behavior.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive shedding could harm high-value customers. Mitigation: tenant priority labels, capped borrowing, and manual override with SLO-exempt tag.
Risk: model heterogeneity makes confidence proxies inconsistent. Mitigation: fallback proxies and conservative defaults; document per-model mapping.
Risk: Bayesian model complexity slow to converge for low-volume tenants. Mitigation: hierarchical priors and pooled statistics; treat low-volume tenants as 'cold' and apply smoothing.
